items.title: Section: A Lamp and Its Light — Scripture Itself Proves Mind and Mental Factors Co-Arise

items.zh: 又違教故，唯心實有，不應道理。違何等教？謂如經言：貪瞋癡等惱染其心，令不解脫。問：此中何所相違？答：若唯有心，二不俱有，是即貪等應不依識。若汝復謂以識為先，亦不應理，無差別過，前已說故。又復經言：與觸俱生受、想、思等。又餘經說：如是諸法恒共和合，非不和合；不可說言如是諸法而可分析，令別殊異。又佛世尊為欲成立此和合義，說燈明喻。是故不可離彼俱生而說和合。
items.en: Furthermore, claiming mind alone is real contradicts scripture. As scripture says: craving, aversion, and delusion afflict and defile the mind, preventing liberation. If only mind existed, with nothing else co-arising, craving and the rest could not depend on consciousness at all. Scripture further says: the meeting of the three gives rise to contact, together with which feeling, perception, and volition arise as well. Other scripture says these phenomena are constantly, inseparably conjoined, never to be analytically separated. The Buddha himself, to establish this same inseparability, spoke the simile of a lamp and its light. Hence one cannot speak of their being conjoined apart from their arising together.

items.zh: 雖復經言：如是六界，說名士夫。然密意說，故無過失。問：此中有何密意？答：唯欲顯說色、動、心所最勝所依，當知是名此經密意。復有違彼聖教可得。何等聖教？

items.title: Section: Milk, Yogurt, and Clarified Butter — And a Sick Monk Healed by Realising There Was Never a Self to Lose

items.zh: 謂世尊言：乳、酪、生酥三譬喻故。或有處所，麁四大種以之為我；或有處所，有色意生；或有處所，無色想生。如是經意，豈唯大種、或唯有心、唯有想耶？是故當知，如是等經皆有密意。故名所攝四無色蘊，心與心所更互相應，道理成就。中嗢拕南曰：五種性不成，分位差過失，因緣無別故，與聖教相違。
items.en:
As the World-Honoured One said, through the three similes of milk, yogurt, and fresh butter: in one place the coarse elements are taken as self; in another, a mind-generated body arises; in another, formless perception gives rise to existence. Does this scripture's own intent really mean only the elements, or only mind, or only perception exist? One should therefore know all such scriptures carry a hidden intent. Hence it is established that mind and the mental factors subsumed under the name-aggregates mutually correspond. A summary verse: the fivefold structure fails, the positional-phase theory carries faults, no differentiated cause can be found, and it contradicts scripture.
[From the story of the monk Assaji] The Buddha said: is this body you? No. Is there some other you apart from it? No. Do you dwell within it? No. Does it belong to you? No. The Buddha said: since form is thus without self, so too are feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. The essential point of renunciation is permanently severing craving, aversion, and delusion, not merely meditative absorption.

items.title: Section: A New Beginning — The Eighteen Elements, and What Actually Constitutes the Eye-Element

items.zh: 如是已決擇蘊事善巧。界事善巧今當決擇。問：何等是眼界？答：若眼未斷，或復斷已命根攝受。如眼界，乃至意識界及法界一分，當知亦爾。問：何等是色界？答：若色根增上所生，若彼於此為增上，是名色界。如色界，乃至觸界，當知亦爾。問：此十八界，幾是實有？幾是假有？答：實有者，或十七、或十二。
items.en: Having now fully decided the skilful understanding of the aggregates, the skilful understanding of the elements shall now be decided. Question: what constitutes the eye-element? Answer: the seed not yet severed, or, even if severed, still sustained by the continuing life faculty. As with the eye-element, so too the ear, up through the mental-consciousness element and a portion of the phenomena-element. Question: what constitutes the visible-form element? Answer: the faculty's own empowering influence, and that same faculty's own seed empowering form's arising. As with visible form, so too sound, up through the tactile element. Question: how many of these eighteen elements are genuinely real, and how many merely provisional? Answer: seventeen are real, or alternatively twelve.

items.title: Section: A Young Monk's Joyful Death — The Four-Cornered Logic of Eye and Eye-Element

items.zh: 六為一故；一為六故。此約世俗安立道理。問：若有眼亦眼界耶？設有眼界亦眼耶？答：應作四句。或有眼非眼界，謂阿羅漢最後眼。是名初句。或有眼界非眼，謂生有色界，若眼未生，或生已失，或不得眼，或眼無間滅；若諸異生生無色界。是第二句。或有眼亦眼界，謂除爾所相。是第三句。或有無眼亦無眼界，謂阿羅漢眼已失壞，或不生眼，若生無色界，或於無餘依涅槃界已般涅槃。是第四句。
items.en: Six counted as one, or one opened into six. This is established according to conventional convention. Question: does possessing an eye entail possessing eye-element, and does possessing eye-element entail possessing an eye? Answer: four possibilities apply. Some possess an eye without eye-element — an arhat's very last eye. Some possess eye-element without an eye — as when, born in a realm possessing form, the eye has not yet arisen, or has been lost after arising, or is not obtained, or has just ceased; or ordinary beings born in the formless realm. Some possess both — all other ordinary cases. And some possess neither — an arhat whose eye is already destroyed, or already in the formless realm and liberated, or already entered final nirvāṇa.

items.title: Section: Extending the Four Corners — Why the Body Alone Cannot Be Missing, and Sound's Own Intermittent Nature

items.zh: 如眼界，一切內界隨其所應，當知亦爾。身界應分別，謂無先來不生身者。餘隨所應，當具宣說。於四外界，隨其所應，亦當具說。若聲、聲界，正宣擊時當言俱有；若不宣擊，當言隨逐餘界，唯界、非聲。
items.en: As with the eye-element, so too should all internal elements be understood, each accordingly. The body-element requires special distinction, since there has never been a case of a body simply failing to arise from the start. The rest, as appropriate, should be fully explained. Regarding the four external elements, this too should be fully explained as appropriate. Regarding sound and the sound-element: when actually spoken or struck, both are present together; when not, it should be said to follow along with the remaining element — only the element, not sound.

items.zh: 問：此十八界，幾是同分？幾彼同分？

items.title: Section: Shared Category or Not — And Why the Buddha Alone Can Judge Where a Being Is Truly Headed

items.zh: 答：有識眼界，名為同分；所餘眼界，名彼同分。如眼界，乃至身界亦爾。唯根所攝內諸界中，思量同分及彼同分；非於色等外諸界中。當知法界諸有所緣，如心界說；諸無所緣，如色等說。問：幾界合而能取？幾界不合能取？答：六，合能取；四，不合能取；五及一少分，非能取；一界，若合不合，二俱能取。問：幾唯所取，非能取？幾亦所取，亦能取耶？答：一切皆所取。謂五及一少分，唯所取；十二及一少分，亦是能取。問：幾由助伴故能取？幾獨能取耶？答：十及一少分，由助伴故能取；一及一少分，獨能取。
items.en: Answer: an eye-element actively accompanied by consciousness shares the common category; the remaining eye-element is called its similar counterpart. As with the eye-element, so too through the body-element. Answer: six grasp only through contact; four grasp only from a distance; five, plus a portion of one, never grasp at all; and one element grasps in both ways, whether in contact or not.

items.title: Section: A Bold Claim Earns the Buddha's Praise, and Which Elements Belong to Which Realm

items.zh: 問：幾唯欲界繫？答：四。問：幾唯色界繫？答：無。問：幾唯無色界繫？答：亦無。問：幾唯欲色界繫？答：十一。
items.en: Question: how many belong exclusively to the desire realm? Answer: four. Question: how many belong exclusively to the form realm? Answer: none. Question: how many belong exclusively to the formless realm? Answer: also none. Question: how many belong jointly to the desire and form realms? Answer: eleven.

blocks.text: Scripture confirms that mind and its factors arise together, like a lamp and its light. Then a new topic: the eighteen elements.

Scripture says greed defiles the mind, that contact arises with feeling, and gives the simile of the lamp. Master Cháng Bǎi: greed and the rest are separate things from mind. Being "conjoined" requires several things arising together.
Scriptures that seem to say otherwise have a hidden intent. Master Cháng Bǎi: "hidden intent" means not stated openly.
Master Cháng Bǎi: 界 means cause: the seeds of things in the store-consciousness. Seventeen or twelve elements are real, depending on how the consciousnesses are counted.
Master Cháng Bǎi: an ordinary being born in the formless heavens has the seed of the eye but no eye: element without eye.
No being lacks a body from the start. Sound is present only when spoken or struck; otherwise only its seed accompanies other elements.
Master Cháng Bǎi: when consciousness works with the eye, the eye is "concordant"; when idle, "similar to the concordant". Mental consciousness takes objects with or without contact.
Smell, taste, and nose- and tongue-consciousness exist only in the desire realm, where there is solid food.
"Element" means seed. The eighteen elements are not eighteen things, but eighteen kinds of potential.

quiz.q: What conclusion does the treatise reach on mind and mental factors among the name-aggregates (§32)?
options: mind and mental factors mutually correspond, as established
mind alone is real, factors being its phases, the treatise finally affirming this school
factors are real, and mind provisional
neither mind nor factors exist
quiz.why: The treatise concludes that scriptures seeming to say otherwise have a hidden intent, and so mind and mental factors correspond. Master Cháng Bǎi: hidden intent means not stated openly. Note the English "carry a hidden dimension" is weaker than 密意, and the rival position is the one refuted in §29–32.

quiz.q: Which scriptures prove separate factors, and what does the lamp simile show?
options: a single discourse; the lamp shows mind comes before factors, lamp first and light later
outsiders' texts; the lamp means wisdom
greed and the rest defile mind; contact arises with feeling and the rest; mind is like a lamp and factors like its light, simultaneous
the Vinaya; the lamp means discipline
quiz.why: The treatise cites scripture that greed and the rest defile the mind, that contact arises with feeling and the rest, and the lamp simile. Master Cháng Bǎi: greed and the rest are thus separate phenomena, not phases of mind; mind is like a lamp and factors like the light it gives, present together. So factors are simultaneous with mind.

quiz.q: The English has "one cannot speak of their co-arising while denying they are conjoined." What is the problem?
options: it reverses the structure: the Chinese says one cannot speak of being conjoined apart from co-arising; this proves factors exist alongside
no problem: the two wordings mean the same, the English fitting the Chinese fully with no need of change
the Chinese says one can, the English adding a negative
the Chinese has no 俱生
quiz.why: The Chinese says being conjoined cannot be spoken of apart from co-arising: there must be several things arising together for there to be a union. Master Cháng Bǎi: this shows mind and factors exist at one time, proving factors have their own substance. The English reverses this, which loses the force of the argument against mind alone.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define the eye-element?
options: only an eye now seeing, the element ceasing when the eyes close and existing only in seeing
the form seen by eye-consciousness
the matter of the eyeball
the eye not yet severed, or, if severed, still sustained by the life faculty
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 界 means cause, the seeds of phenomena in the store-consciousness; and if the seed for a future eye is already severed but the life faculty continues, it is still called the eye-element, as with an arhat in nirvāṇa with remainder. The English adds "seed," following one reading, while the Chinese has only 眼.

quiz.q: How do "seventeen or twelve" real elements count, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi add for the Mahāyāna?
options: the mental element and six consciousnesses open and close, one side provisional; this is conventional, the Mahāyāna holding all eighteen real
seventeen are real, the eighteenth being space, the Mahāyāna likewise admitting only seventeen, as the treatise says
twelve are the twelve links; seventeen the seventeen stages
seventeen for the desire realm, twelve for the form realm
quiz.why: The treatise says seventeen or twelve are real, six being counted as one or one opened into six, on conventional reasoning. Master Cháng Bǎi: the six consciousness elements are provisional in one way of counting because the mental element opens into them; but the Mahāyāna says the mental element is of two kinds, so all eighteen are real.

quiz.q: The English has "as when born in the formless realm" for 若諸異生生無色界. What is the problem with dropping 異生?
options: no problem: all born there alike have the eye-element, 異生 being superfluous, so the English rightly omits it
ordinary beings there have the seed but no eye; noble ones there fall under the fourth corner, so dropping 異生 conflicts with it
異生 means animals, omitted by the English
異生 means outsiders, to be added
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: an ordinary being born in the formless heavens has the seed of the eye faculty but no eye, and this is element without eye. A noble one there, whose seed is severed, belongs under neither. So the word 異生 is what keeps the second corner distinct from the fourth. The English also drops "born where there is form" and two other cases.

quiz.q: Why can the body-element not be treated in four corners like the eye?
options: because the body-element matters less than the eye, passed over merely to save space
because the body-element is provisional
because the body-element exists only in the desire realm
without a body there is no life; until death the body faculty is surely present, while one may lose an eye and live
quiz.why: The treatise says the body-element needs special distinction, since no being has failed to have a body from the start. Master Cháng Bǎi: without a body there is no life-form, so before death the body faculty is surely present; unlike the eye, which can be lost after birth without preventing survival.

quiz.q: What is the key point of sound and the sound-element?
options: sound is always present though sometimes unheard; the element exists only when struck, with no seed otherwise
both are present when spoken or struck; otherwise only the element, not sound
neither sound nor its element exists
the sound-element is the ear faculty
quiz.why: The treatise says both are present when sound is spoken or struck; when not, the element accompanies other elements, element only and not sound. Master Cháng Bǎi: then there is only the seed of sound and no manifest sound. The English drops "accompanying other elements."

quiz.q: The English has "stands apart in its own category" for 彼同分. How does the lecture explain it?
options: with consciousness it is 同分; seeing without seeing, not discriminating form, is 彼同分; the English comes close to "not sharing"
彼同分 is another person's eye, unrelated to oneself, so "stands apart" is exact, meaning someone else's eye
彼同分 is an arhat's eye-element
彼同分 is the divine eye
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when consciousness works with the eye faculty it is 同分; in seeing without seeing, not discriminating form, it is 彼同分. So it is the same faculty, similar to the working one. "Stands apart in its own category" reads like "not sharing," and fascicle 53 used "discordant" for this very term.

quiz.q: Which element grasps whether in contact or not, and why?
options: the eye-element, which sees near and far, unlimited by distance, the only such faculty
the body-element, touching or not
the ear-element, hearing near or far
the mental-consciousness element, not limited by contact or its absence
quiz.why: The treatise sorts elements as grasping through contact, without contact, not grasping, and either way. Master Cháng Bǎi: mental consciousness is not limited by contact, and can take objects either way; and one observes the grasped to break clinging to objects as self, and the grasper to break clinging to the experiencing mind as self. The English "independently" adds a sense.
